title: marketing-modes
universal_lens: A finite mode algebra M = {m_i} with binary hook predicate H: M → {0,1} and schema validation operator Σ: M → {valid, stale}. The system forms a commutative diagram where deduplication D: URL → Entity induces idempotent projection D∘D = D, and avatar typing A: Entity → {preset, custom}×ID partitions the state space.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian mode selection: posterior P(m|context) ∝ P(context|m)P(m) where likelihood encodes hook compatibility H(m) and context labels (tutorial, unboxing, review). Conformal prediction set C_α = {m: p-value(m) > α} guarantees coverage over schema drift Σ_t. Deduplication D yields exchangeable entity sequence for sequential testing.
gse_mapping: State machine S = (M, Σ, D, A) with transitions: fetch URL → validate Σ(m) → generate → deduplicate D. Hook predicate H(m) gates action space A_m = {hook_id, setting_id} if H(m)=1 else ∅. Wild_card mode induces stochastic transition kernel K(m'|m) for exploration. Avatar type partitions observation space O = O_preset ∪ O_custom.

primitives.name: Mode Taxonomy Classification Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: | `--mode` slug | Human-readable label | Hook/setting | Best for | |---|---|---|---| | `ugc` | UGC | ✅ | Default.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: \mathcal{M}: dimensionless mode set (cardinality 9); m_i: dimensionless mode identifier; i: index ∈ ℕ
primitives.assumptions: Modes are mutually exclusive and collectively exhaustive for marketing_studio_video; schema version fixed at query time; hook/setting validity is binary per mode
primitives.breakdown_regime: Schema drift when live schema adds/removes modes; validation fails if local mode set ≠ remote schema; wild_card mode non-deterministic breaks exhaustive classification

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE discrete action space A = {a_i} where each mode m_i ↦ action a_i with preconditions H(m_i) and reward context R(context|m_i). GSI: mode selection as categorical distribution with Dirichlet prior.
layer2.telemetry: Mode distribution entropy H(M); schema validation failure rate; wild_card selection frequency

primitives.name: Hook/Setting Validity Predicate
primitives.verbatim_quote: | The "Hook/setting" column shows whether `--hook_id` and `--setting_id` are valid for that mode.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: H: dimensionless predicate (0/1); m ∈ ℳ: mode identifier; hook_id, setting_id: dimensionless parameter identifiers
primitives.assumptions: Binary validity per mode; no partial validity; hook/setting validity independent of avatar type or URL
primitives.breakdown_regime: Schema evolution adds hook/setting parameters to previously invalid modes; context-dependent validity (e.g., avatar type gates hook availability)

layer2.mapping: GSE: H(m) defines action mask for RL policy π(a|m) = 0 if H(m)=0. GSI: likelihood factor P(hook_valid|m) = H(m) in Bayesian mode selection. Kernel K_H(m'|m) = δ_{m,m'}H(m) for constrained transitions.
layer2.telemetry: Hook/setting usage rate per mode; validation error count for invalid hook attempts; mode-switching frequency when H(m)=0

primitives.name: Live Schema Validation Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: The live schema is the source of truth, so run `higgsfield model get marketing_studio_video` if validation fails.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Σ_t: dimensionless validation operator at time t; ℳ_local, ℳ_remote(t): dimensionless mode sets; t: time (seconds since epoch)
primitives.assumptions: Remote schema authoritative; local cache may stale; validation is equality check of mode sets; network latency negligible
primitives.breakdown_regime: Network partition prevents remote fetch; schema versioning without backward compatibility; concurrent schema mutations during validation

layer2.mapping: GSE: Σ_t as environment observation function O(s_t) = valid/stale. GSI: conformal prediction with nonconformity score α = 1{Σ_t = stale}; guarantees P(Σ_t = valid) ≥ 1-α under exchangeability of schema versions.
layer2.telemetry: Schema staleness duration; validation latency p99; mode set symmetric difference size |ℳ_local Δ ℳ_remote|

primitives.name: Entity Deduplication Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: - `avatars`: array of `{id, type}` where `type` is `preset` or `custom`.
primitives.latex: D: \mathcal{U} \to \mathcal{E}, \quad D(u) = \begin{cases} e_{existing} & \exists e \in \mathcal{E}_{non-failed}: e.url = u \\ e_{new} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}, \quad D \circ D = D
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: D: deduplication operator; 𝒰: URL space (dimensionless strings); ℰ: entity space; e: entity with fields {id, url, status}; status ∈ {pending, success, failed}
primitives.assumptions: URL is canonical key; non-failed entities reusable; failed entities not reused; deduplication idempotent; no TTL expiration
primitives.breakdown_regime: URL collision for distinct content; entity state corruption; distributed backend consistency lag; failed entity later succeeds (race condition)

layer2.mapping: GSE: D as state transition filter reducing state space cardinality. GSI: D induces exchangeable sequence for sequential Bayesian updating; conformal p-values computed on deduplicated entities. Isomorphic to GSE idempotent projection in state estimation.
layer2.telemetry: Deduplication rate (1 - |ℰ_unique|/|ℰ_requests|); entity reuse latency; failed entity resurrection rate

The source defines a finite mode algebra ℳ with 9 elements, each carrying a binary hook predicate H(m) and contextual fitness label. The live schema validation Σ_t creates a temporal dimension where ℳ_local may diverge from ℳ_remote(t), inducing a staleness detection problem. Entity deduplication D: 𝒰 → ℰ is an idempotent operator (D∘D=D) that partitions requests into equivalence classes by URL, reusing non-failed entities. Avatar typing A: ℰ → {preset,custom}×ID further partitions the entity space. The wild_card mode breaks deterministic classification by introducing a stochastic kernel K(m'|m). The system forms a commutative diagram: fetch → validate Σ_t → select mode m → check H(m) → generate → deduplicate D. Breakdown regimes: schema drift (Σ_t=stale), hook invalidation (H(m) changes), URL collision (D non-injective), wild_card non-determinism. The primitives capture the algebraic structure (ℳ, H), temporal validation (Σ_t), and state reduction (D, A).
